```{r stage4-join}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 4. ADU-TO-PARCEL JOIN (with the Grandfathered ADU tag)
# Joins projects to properties, then assigns tract, CPA and property type from
# the property. Tags single-family parcels coded as having an ADU but holding no
# project as older_adu.
# Stops the knit if: the match rate falls below 99%.
# =============================================================================
if (run4) {
  pc <- parcel_class %>% filter(!is.na(AIN), AIN != "") %>% distinct(AIN, .keep_all = TRUE)
  # Projects permitted 2010 to 2016 are joined the same way and kept apart
  p <- bind_rows(projects %>% mutate(pre2017 = FALSE), projects_pre %>% mutate(pre2017 = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(apn10 = str_trim(apn), pin_n = str_squish(pin), prop_id = NA_character_, join_step = NA_character_)

  # Step 1: permit APN = parcel AIN
  i1 <- which(p$apn10 %in% pc$AIN)
  p$prop_id[i1] <- p$apn10[i1]; p$join_step[i1] <- "1. APN"

  # Step 2: PIN_NBR (internal spaces collapsed) -> City parcel PIN -> BPP -> AIN
  cp_layer <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(params$path_city_parcels))
  city_pin <- st_read(params$path_city_parcels, quiet = TRUE,
                      query = sprintf('SELECT PIN, BPP FROM "%s"', cp_layer)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry() %>%
    transmute(pin_n = str_squish(PIN), bpp = str_trim(BPP)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(pin_n), pin_n != "", str_detect(coalesce(bpp, ""), "^[0-9]{10}$")) %>%  # skip masked BPPs
    distinct(pin_n, .keep_all = TRUE)
  i2 <- which(is.na(p$prop_id) & !is.na(p$pin_n))
  bpp2 <- city_pin$bpp[match(p$pin_n[i2], city_pin$pin_n)]
  ok2 <- !is.na(bpp2) & bpp2 %in% pc$AIN
  n_pin_bpp_outside <- sum(!is.na(bpp2) & !(bpp2 %in% pc$AIN))   # BPP is not a City parcel AIN
  p$prop_id[i2[ok2]] <- bpp2[ok2]; p$join_step[i2[ok2]] <- "2. City PIN"
  n_city_pins <- nrow(city_pin); rm(city_pin)

  # Step 3: coordinates -> containing parcel, else nearest parcel within 50 ft
  if (!file.exists(params$path_parcel_shp))
    unzip(params$path_parcel_zip, exdir = dirname(dirname(params$path_parcel_shp)))
  layer <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(params$path_parcel_shp))
  read_ains <- function(ains) {   # County polygons for a set of AINs
    if (!length(ains)) return(st_sf(AIN = character(0), geometry = st_sfc(crs = crs_ft)))
    st_read(params$path_parcel_shp, quiet = TRUE,
            query = sprintf('SELECT AIN FROM "%s" WHERE AIN IN (%s)', layer,
                            paste0("'", ains, "'", collapse = ","))) %>%
      to_ft() %>% mutate(AIN = str_trim(AIN))
  }
  i3 <- which(is.na(p$prop_id) & !is.na(p$lat) & !is.na(p$lon) & p$lat != 0 & p$lon != 0)
  n_coord_tried <- length(i3)
  if (length(i3)) {
    pts3 <- st_as_sf(p[i3, c("root", "lon", "lat")], coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = crs_web) %>%
      st_transform(crs_ft)
    near_wkt <- st_as_text(st_union(st_buffer(pts3, 60)))
    cand <- st_read(params$path_parcel_shp, quiet = TRUE,
                    query = sprintf('SELECT AIN FROM "%s"', layer), wkt_filter = near_wkt) %>%
      to_ft() %>% mutate(AIN = str_trim(AIN)) %>% filter(AIN %in% pc$AIN)
    okv <- st_is_valid(cand); if (any(!okv | is.na(okv))) cand <- st_make_valid(cand)
    hit <- st_intersects(pts3, cand)
    in_aid <- vapply(hit, function(h) if (length(h)) cand$AIN[h[1]] else NA_character_, "")
    miss <- which(is.na(in_aid))
    near_aid <- rep(NA_character_, length(in_aid))
    if (length(miss) && nrow(cand)) {
      nf <- st_nearest_feature(pts3[miss, ], cand)
      d  <- as.numeric(st_distance(pts3[miss, ], cand[nf, ], by_element = TRUE))
      near_aid[miss] <- ifelse(d <= 50, cand$AIN[nf], NA_character_)
    }
    p$prop_id[i3]   <- coalesce(in_aid, near_aid)
    p$join_step[i3] <- case_when(!is.na(in_aid) ~ "3. Coordinates, inside parcel",
                                 !is.na(near_aid) ~ "3. Coordinates, nearest within 50 ft",
                                 TRUE ~ NA_character_)
  }
  p$join_step[is.na(p$prop_id)] <- "4. Unmatched (permit CPA text)"

  # Inherit parcel attributes
  adu_all <- p %>%
    left_join(pc %>% select(prop_id = AIN, parcel_cpa = cpa, ct20, tract_cpa, land_use,
                            lot_sqft, hillside_fire, in_roll, use_type, pt_x, pt_y),
              by = "prop_id") %>%
    mutate(cpa = coalesce(parcel_cpa, cpa_text),
           property_type = case_when(
             !is.na(prop_id) & land_use == "Single-family" ~ "Single-family",
             !is.na(prop_id) & str_starts(land_use, "Multi-family") ~ "Multi-family",
             !is.na(prop_id) ~ "Other",
             sub_type %in% "Apartment" ~ "Multi-family",   # fallback
             TRUE ~ "Unknown"))

  adu <- filter(adu_all, !pre2017); adu_pre <- filter(adu_all, pre2017)
  is_v11 <- !p$pre2017 & p$source_rule != "work-description wording"   # the set before the wording rule

  # older_adu (Assessor-only): SFR parcels coded 6 that the full join ties to no
  # permitted project, 2010 to 2016 projects included. older_v11 is the earlier
  # definition (2017-on flag and use-type projects only), kept for the checks.
  parcel_class <- parcel_class %>%
    mutate(older_adu = adu_code6 & !(AIN %in% adu_all$prop_id),
           older_v11 = adu_code6 & !(AIN %in% adu_all$prop_id[is_v11]))
  older_counts <- parcel_class %>% filter(older_adu) %>% count(cpa, ct20, name = "older_adu")
  older_counts_v11 <- parcel_class %>% filter(older_v11) %>% count(cpa, name = "older_adu")

  # ---- Diagnostics for the benchmarks ---------
  # (a) Permit APNs that are County AINs outside the City parcel table
  un_apn <- unique(p$apn10[!(p$apn10 %in% pc$AIN) & str_detect(coalesce(p$apn10, ""), "^[0-9]{10}$")])
  apn_outside_set <- read_ains(un_apn)$AIN
  n_apn_outside <- sum(p$apn10[is_v11] %in% apn_outside_set)
  # (a2) PIN-step BPPs that are County AINs outside the City parcel table, for
  #      projects the target's PIN step would have seen
  county_bpp <- read_ains(unique(bpp2[!is.na(bpp2) & !(bpp2 %in% pc$AIN)]))$AIN
  n_pin_bpp_county_outside <- sum(is_v11[i2] & !is.na(bpp2) & bpp2 %in% county_bpp & !(p$apn10[i2] %in% apn_outside_set))
  # (b) Tagged parcels that contain the point of a project already placed by
  #     APN or PIN (an earlier test removed these too)
  tag_cand <- parcel_class$AIN[parcel_class$older_v11]
  tag_poly <- read_ains(tag_cand)
  allpts <- adu_all[is_v11, ] %>% filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), lat != 0, lon != 0) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = crs_web) %>% st_transform(crs_ft)
  hit_tag <- unique(tag_poly$AIN[unlist(st_intersects(allpts, tag_poly))])
  hit_tag_cpa <- parcel_class %>% filter(AIN %in% hit_tag) %>% count(cpa)

  saveRDS(list(adu = adu, adu_pre = adu_pre, older_counts = older_counts, older_counts_v11 = older_counts_v11,
               n_code6_with_any = sum(parcel_class$adu_code6 & parcel_class$AIN %in% adu_all$prop_id),
               n_apn_outside = n_apn_outside, n_pin_bpp_outside = n_pin_bpp_outside,
               n_pin_bpp_county_outside = n_pin_bpp_county_outside,
               hit_tag = hit_tag, hit_tag_cpa = hit_tag_cpa,
               n_code6 = sum(parcel_class$adu_code6),
               n_code6_with_project = sum(parcel_class$adu_code6 & parcel_class$AIN %in% adu_all$prop_id[is_v11]),
               n_city_pins = n_city_pins, n_coord_tried = n_coord_tried), f_joined)
}
s4 <- readRDS(f_joined)
adu <- s4$adu; adu_pre <- s4$adu_pre; older_counts <- s4$older_counts
adu_v11 <- filter(adu, source_rule != "work-description wording")   # the set before the wording rule
adu_focus <- adu %>% filter(cpa %in% focus_cpas)
if (!"older_adu" %in% names(parcel_class))
  parcel_class <- parcel_class %>%
    mutate(older_adu = adu_code6 & !(AIN %in% c(adu$prop_id, adu_pre$prop_id)))
# Step 9. Grandfathered ADUs: one completed unit per single-family parcel the roll codes as
# having an ADU and that holds no permitted ADU. No permit, so no dates and no issue year.
adu_gf <- st_drop_geometry(parcel_class) %>% filter(older_adu) %>%
  transmute(root = paste0("ASR-", AIN), prop_id = AIN, cpa, parcel_cpa = cpa, ct20, tract_cpa, land_use, lot_sqft, hillside_fire,
            in_roll, use_type, pt_x, pt_y, property_type = "Single-family", units = 1, status = "Completed", completed = TRUE,
            source_rule = "assessor use code", source_tag = factor(tag_levels[3], levels = tag_levels), join_step = "Assessor record", n_chains = 1L)
qa_add(4, "Grandfathered ADUs: one row per parcel, none on a parcel with a permitted ADU", fmt(sum(parcel_class$older_adu)), fmt(nrow(adu_gf)),
       !any(duplicated(adu_gf$prop_id)) && !any(adu_gf$prop_id %in% c(adu$prop_id, adu_pre$prop_id)) && nrow(adu_gf) == sum(parcel_class$older_adu), stop_if_fail = TRUE)

## Joining ADUs to parcels, tracts and CPAs

Each permitted project joins to a County parcel in three steps: the permit APN to the parcel AIN; then, if unmatched, the permit `PIN_NBR` to the City parcel file's PIN, whose BPP gives the APN; then, if still unmatched, the parcel containing the project's coordinates, or the nearest parcel within 50 ft. A project inherits its parcel's AIN (`prop_id`), CPA, tract, land use class, lot size and hillside-fire flag, so ADU counts and lot counts share one parcel ID. A project that no step places keeps its permit CPA text for CPA totals, with property type "unknown". Older permitted projects are joined by the same three steps. Grandfathered ADUs (step 9) start from the parcel, so they need no join: a single-family parcel coded 6 in the 2026 roll is grandfathered when the join ties no permitted ADU to it.

```{r stage4-tables}

      note = paste0("County parcels exported August 2, 2025; City parcel file for the PIN step. LADBS permitted ADUs, ", ladbs_window, "."))

## ACS variables and margins of error

Community data come from the American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates for census tracts in Los Angeles County, joined to the crosswalk on GEOID (never on the tract name). Counts are summed across a CPA's tracts; rates and averages are recomputed from the summed counts, never averaged across tracts. Margins of error use the tidycensus helpers, which apply the Census Bureau's approximation formulas: `moe_sum()` for sums and differences, `moe_prop()` for shares whose numerator is part of the denominator, and `moe_ratio()` for the vacancy rates and averages. The Census Bureau warns these approximations weaken as more estimates are combined, so CPA margins of error are approximate. An estimate is flagged **low reliability** when its coefficient of variation, (MOE ÷ 1.645) ÷ estimate, exceeds 30%.

```{r stage5-acs}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 5. ACS
# Pulls tract estimates and margins of error, keeps crosswalk tracts, aggregates
# to CPA. The key is read from .Renviron and never printed.
# Stops the knit if: a crosswalk tract is missing from the pull, or the five
# household counts disagree in any tract.
# =============================================================================

  rb_all = "B25070_001", rb_nc = "B25070_011",
  rb_30 = c("B25070_007", "B25070_008", "B25070_009", "B25070_010"), rb_50 = "B25070_010",
  hu = "DP04_0001", occ = "DP04_0002", vac = "DP04_0003",
  ed_univ = "B15003_001", ed_ba = c("B15003_022", "B15003_023", "B15003_024", "B15003_025"),
  agg_inc = "B19025_001", hh_b11001 = "B11001_001", agg_rent = "B25065_001", rent_cash = "B25063_002",
  v_rent = "B25004_002", v_rented = "B25004_003", v_sale = "B25004_004", v_sold = "B25004_005",
  emp_occ = "DP03_0026", occ_wc = c("DP03_0028", "DP03_0029", "DP03_0030", "DP03_0031"),
  emp_ind = "DP03_0032", ind_wc = c(sprintf("DP03_%04d", 33:38), "DP03_0043", "DP03_0044"))

clean_acs <- function(d) d %>%   # ACS sentinel values to NA
  mutate(estimate = if_else(!is.na(estimate) & estimate <= -1e8, NA_real_, estimate),
         moe = case_when(moe == -555555555 ~ 0,            # controlled estimate: no sampling error
                         !is.na(moe) & moe < 0 ~ NA_real_,
                         TRUE ~ moe))

# ---- Components and measures for any grouping (tract or CPA) -----------------
component_table <- function(d, group) {
  imap_dfr(comp, function(vars, nm) {
    d %>% filter(variable %in% vars) %>% group_by(group = .data[[group]]) %>%
      summarise(estimate = sum(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
                moe = moe_sum(moe, estimate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
      mutate(comp = nm)
  })
}
rss <- function(...) sqrt(rowSums(cbind(...)^2))
build_measures <- function(ct) {
  w  <- ct %>% select(group, comp, estimate) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = comp, values_from = estimate)
  wm <- ct %>% select(group, comp, moe) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = comp, values_from = moe)
  E <- function(x) w[[x]]; M <- function(x) wm[[x]]
  rb_comp_e <- E("rb_all") - E("rb_nc"); rb_comp_m <- rss(M("rb_all"), M("rb_nc"))
  ov_den_e <- E("own_b25003") + E("v_sale") + E("v_sold"); ov_den_m <- rss(M("own_b25003"), M("v_sale"), M("v_sold"))
  rv_den_e <- E("rent_b25003") + E("v_rent") + E("v_rented"); rv_den_m <- rss(M("rent_b25003"), M("v_rent"), M("v_rented"))
  cnt <- function(lbl, e, m) tibble(group = w$group, measure = lbl, type = "count", estimate = e, moe = m)
  prp <- function(lbl, ne, nm, de, dm) tibble(group = w$group, measure = lbl, type = "rate",
                                               estimate = ne / de, moe = moe_prop(ne, de, nm, dm))
  rat <- function(lbl, ne, nm, de, dm, type = "average") tibble(group = w$group, measure = lbl, type = type,
                                                                 estimate = ne / de, moe = moe_ratio(ne, de, nm, dm))
  bind_rows(
    cnt("Total population", E("pop"), M("pop")),
    cnt("Total households", E("hh"), M("hh")),
    cnt("Owner households", E("own"), M("own")),
    cnt("Renter households", E("rent"), M("rent")),
    cnt("Owner households that moved in 2020 or later", E("own_moved20"), M("own_moved20")),
    cnt("Owner households that moved in 2023 or later", E("own_moved23"), M("own_moved23")),
    cnt("Households with poverty status", E("pov_univ"), M("pov_univ")),
    cnt("Households below poverty", E("pov_below"), M("pov_below")),
    cnt("Latino households", E("lat_hh"), M("lat_hh")),
    cnt("Latino owner households", E("lat_own"), M("lat_own")),
    cnt("Black households", E("blk_hh"), M("blk_hh")),
    cnt("Black owner households", E("blk_own"), M("blk_own")),
    cnt("Non-Hispanic white households", E("wht_hh"), M("wht_hh")),
    cnt("Non-Hispanic white owner households", E("wht_own"), M("wht_own")),
    cnt("Renter households with a computed rent burden", rb_comp_e, rb_comp_m),
    cnt("Rent-burdened households", E("rb_30"), M("rb_30")),
    cnt("Severely rent-burdened households", E("rb_50"), M("rb_50")),
    cnt("Total housing units", E("hu"), M("hu")),
    cnt("Occupied housing units", E("occ"), M("occ")),
    cnt("Vacant housing units", E("vac"), M("vac")),
    cnt("Adults 25 and over", E("ed_univ"), M("ed_univ")),
    cnt("Adults 25 and over with a bachelor's degree or higher", E("ed_ba"), M("ed_ba")),
    rat("Average household income", E("agg_inc"), M("agg_inc"), E("hh_b11001"), M("hh_b11001")),
    rat("Average gross rent", E("agg_rent"), M("agg_rent"), E("rent_cash"), M("rent_cash")),
    prp("Homeownership rate", E("own"), M("own"), E("hh"), M("hh")),
    prp("Latino homeownership rate", E("lat_own"), M("lat_own"), E("lat_hh"), M("lat_hh")),
    prp("Black homeownership rate", E("blk_own"), M("blk_own"), E("blk_hh"), M("blk_hh")),
    prp("Non-Hispanic white homeownership rate", E("wht_own"), M("wht_own"), E("wht_hh"), M("wht_hh")),
    prp("Latino share of owner households", E("lat_own"), M("lat_own"), E("own_b25003"), M("own_b25003")),
    prp("Black share of owner households", E("blk_own"), M("blk_own"), E("own_b25003"), M("own_b25003")),
    prp("Non-Hispanic white share of owner households", E("wht_own"), M("wht_own"), E("own_b25003"), M("own_b25003")),
    prp("Share of owners that moved in 2020 or later", E("own_moved20"), M("own_moved20"), E("own"), M("own")),
    prp("Share of owners that moved in 2023 or later", E("own_moved23"), M("own_moved23"), E("own"), M("own")),
    prp("Household poverty rate", E("pov_below"), M("pov_below"), E("pov_univ"), M("pov_univ")),
    prp("Rent-burden rate", E("rb_30"), M("rb_30"), rb_comp_e, rb_comp_m),
    prp("Severe rent-burden rate", E("rb_50"), M("rb_50"), rb_comp_e, rb_comp_m),
    prp("Homeowner vacancy rate", E("v_sale"), M("v_sale"), ov_den_e, ov_den_m),
    prp("Rental vacancy rate", E("v_rent"), M("v_rent"), rv_den_e, rv_den_m),
    prp("Share of adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher", E("ed_ba"), M("ed_ba"), E("ed_univ"), M("ed_univ"))
  ) %>%
    mutate(cv = (moe / 1.645) / estimate,
           low_reliability = !is.na(cv) & is.finite(cv) & cv > 0.30)
}
acs_cpa <- component_table(acs_long, "cpa") %>% build_measures() %>% rename(cpa = group)
acs_tract_meas <- component_table(acs_long, "GEOID") %>% build_measures() %>% rename(GEOID = group)
acs_tract <- acs_wide %>% left_join(select(tract_xwalk, GEOID, CT20, cpa), by = "GEOID")

  mutate(hv = 100 * B25004_004 / (B25003_002 + B25004_004 + B25004_005),

```{r stage5-change}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 5 (part 2). HOMEOWNERSHIP CHANGE, 2015-2019 TO 2020-2024
# The 2015-2019 ACS uses 2010 tracts and the 2020-2024 ACS uses 2020 tracts.
# CPA totals: 2010 tracts are assigned to CPAs by the same 50% rule and summed.
# Tract maps: the Census 2010-to-2020 relationship file links the two; tracts
# that were split or merged are compared as the smallest group of tracts that
# matches in both years. Change = later minus earlier. MOE of a change = root
# sum of squares of the two periods' margins; shares use the Census formula for
# a derived proportion in each period first. A change larger than its margin is
# significant at 90%.
# =============================================================================
chg_vars <- c(hh = "B25003_001", own = "B25003_002", blk_hh = "B25003B_001", blk_own = "B25003B_002",
              lat_hh = "B25003I_001", lat_own = "B25003I_002")
f_acs19 <- file.path(dir_derived, "acs_tract_2015_2019_tenure.csv")
if (params$refresh || !file.exists(f_acs19)) {
  census_api_key(Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY"))
  get_acs(geography = "tract", state = "CA", county = "Los Angeles", variables = unname(chg_vars),
          year = 2019, survey = "acs5") %>% clean_acs() %>% select(GEOID, variable, estimate, moe) %>% write_csv(f_acs19)
}
chg_wide <- function(long) long %>% filter(variable %in% chg_vars) %>%
  mutate(nm = names(chg_vars)[match(variable, chg_vars)]) %>% select(GEOID, nm, estimate, moe) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = nm, values_from = c(estimate, moe), names_glue = "{substr(.value, 1, 1)}_{nm}")
t19 <- chg_wide(read_csv(f_acs19, col_types = cols(GEOID = "c", variable = "c", .default = "d")))   # 2010 tracts
t24 <- chg_wide(acs_long_all)                                                                       # 2020 tracts
chg_sum <- function(d, by) d %>% group_by(across(all_of(by))) %>%          # counts add; margins by root sum of squares
  summarise(across(starts_with("e_"), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)), across(starts_with("m_"), ~ sqrt(sum(.x^2, na.rm = TRUE))), .groups = "drop")
p_moe <- function(ne, nm, de, dm) {                                        # Census derived-proportion margin
  p <- ne / de; rad <- nm^2 - p^2 * dm^2
  ifelse(de > 0, sqrt(ifelse(rad >= 0, rad, nm^2 + p^2 * dm^2)) / de, NA_real_)
}
chg_measures <- function(d, id) {                                          # long: one row per unit and measure
  cnt <- function(key, lab, e, m) tibble(unit = d[[id]], key = key, measure = lab, type = "count", est = e, moe = m)
  prp <- function(key, lab, ne, nm, de, dm) tibble(unit = d[[id]], key = key, measure = lab, type = "rate",
                                                   est = ifelse(de > 0, ne / de, NA_real_), moe = p_moe(ne, nm, de, dm))
  bind_rows(
    cnt("hh", "Households", d$e_hh, d$m_hh), cnt("own", "Owner households", d$e_own, d$m_own),
    prp("own_rate", "Homeownership rate", d$e_own, d$m_own, d$e_hh, d$m_hh),
    cnt("blk_hh", "Black households", d$e_blk_hh, d$m_blk_hh), cnt("blk_own", "Black owner households", d$e_blk_own, d$m_blk_own),
    prp("blk_rate", "Share of Black households who own", d$e_blk_own, d$m_blk_own, d$e_blk_hh, d$m_blk_hh),
    prp("blk_shr", "Black share of owner households", d$e_blk_own, d$m_blk_own, d$e_own, d$m_own),
    cnt("lat_hh", "Latino households", d$e_lat_hh, d$m_lat_hh), cnt("lat_own", "Latino owner households", d$e_lat_own, d$m_lat_own),
    prp("lat_rate", "Share of Latino households who own", d$e_lat_own, d$m_lat_own, d$e_lat_hh, d$m_lat_hh),
    prp("lat_shr", "Latino share of owner households", d$e_lat_own, d$m_lat_own, d$e_own, d$m_own))
}
chg_join <- function(m19, m24) inner_join(m19, m24, by = c("unit", "key", "measure", "type"), suffix = c("19", "24")) %>%
  mutate(chg = est24 - est19, chg_moe = sqrt(moe19^2 + moe24^2), sig = !is.na(chg) & !is.na(chg_moe) & abs(chg) > chg_moe)

# ---- CPA totals: 2010 tracts assigned by the same 50% rule ---------------------
tracts10_sf <- st_read(params$path_tracts10, quiet = TRUE) %>% st_make_valid() %>% to_ft() %>%
  mutate(tract_area = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) %>% select(GEOID10 = GEOID, tract_area)
xw10 <- suppressWarnings(st_intersection(tracts10_sf, six_sf)) %>% mutate(int_area = as.numeric(st_area(geometry))) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% mutate(share_in_cpa = int_area / tract_area) %>% filter(share_in_cpa >= 0.5)
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: no 2010 tract is assigned to two CPAs", "0", sum(duplicated(xw10$GEOID10)),
       !any(duplicated(xw10$GEOID10)), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
miss19 <- setdiff(xw10$GEOID10, t19$GEOID)
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: 2010 tracts in the six CPAs missing from the 2015-2019 pull", "0", length(miss19),
       length(miss19) == 0, stop_if_fail = TRUE)
c19 <- chg_sum(t19 %>% inner_join(select(xw10, GEOID = GEOID10, cpa), by = "GEOID"), "cpa")
c24 <- chg_sum(t24 %>% inner_join(select(tract_xwalk, GEOID, cpa), by = "GEOID"), "cpa")
own_chg_cpa <- chg_join(chg_measures(c19, "cpa"), chg_measures(c24, "cpa")) %>% rename(cpa = unit) %>%
  left_join(count(xw10, cpa, name = "tracts10"), by = "cpa") %>% left_join(count(tract_xwalk, cpa, name = "tracts20"), by = "cpa")
chk24 <- own_chg_cpa %>% filter(key == "own") %>%
  inner_join(acs_long %>% filter(variable == "B25003_002") %>% group_by(cpa) %>% summarise(e = sum(estimate)), by = "cpa")
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: 2020-2024 owner households by CPA equal the sum of the crosswalk tracts", "6 CPAs",
       paste(sum(chk24$est24 == chk24$e), "match"), nrow(chk24) == 6 && all(chk24$est24 == chk24$e), stop_if_fail = TRUE)

# ---- Tract groups: smallest sets of tracts that match in both years ------------
rel <- read_delim(params$path_tract_rel, delim = "|", col_types = cols(.default = "c"), progress = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(g20 = GEOID_TRACT_20, g10 = GEOID_TRACT_10, a20 = as.numeric(AREALAND_TRACT_20), a10 = as.numeric(AREALAND_TRACT_10),
            part = as.numeric(AREALAND_PART)) %>%
  filter(str_starts(g20, "06037") | str_starts(g10, "06037"), !is.na(g20), !is.na(g10))
rel_min_share <- 0.05      # a link counts when the shared land is at least 5% of either tract; smaller overlaps are boundary adjustments
links <- rel %>% filter((a20 > 0 & part / a20 >= rel_min_share) | (a10 > 0 & part / a10 >= rel_min_share))
comp_label <- function(a, b) {                       # connected components by repeated minimum labelling
  nodes <- unique(c(a, b)); lab <- setNames(seq_along(nodes), nodes)
  repeat {
    m <- pmin(lab[a], lab[b]); mn <- tapply(c(m, m), c(a, b), min)
    new <- lab; new[names(mn)] <- pmin(new[names(mn)], mn)
    if (all(new == lab)) break
    lab <- new
  }
  lab
}
lab <- comp_label(paste0("n20_", links$g20), paste0("n10_", links$g10))
grp20 <- tibble(GEOID = sub("^n20_", "", names(lab)[str_starts(names(lab), "n20_")]), grp = unname(lab[str_starts(names(lab), "n20_")]))
grp10 <- tibble(GEOID = sub("^n10_", "", names(lab)[str_starts(names(lab), "n10_")]), grp = unname(lab[str_starts(names(lab), "n10_")]))
g19 <- chg_sum(t19 %>% inner_join(grp10, by = "GEOID"), "grp"); g24 <- chg_sum(t24 %>% inner_join(grp20, by = "GEOID"), "grp")
grp_size <- count(grp20, grp, name = "n20") %>% left_join(count(grp10, grp, name = "n10"), by = "grp")
own_chg_grp <- chg_join(chg_measures(g19, "grp"), chg_measures(g24, "grp")) %>% rename(grp = unit)
own_chg_tract <- grp20 %>% left_join(grp_size, by = "grp") %>%            # one row per 2020 tract, with its group's change
  left_join(own_chg_grp %>% filter(key %in% c("own", "lat_own", "blk_own", "lat_shr", "blk_shr", "lat_rate", "blk_rate")) %>%
              select(grp, key, est19, est24, chg, chg_moe, sig) %>%
              pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from = c(est19, est24, chg, chg_moe, sig)), by = "grp")
miss_grp <- setdiff(tract_xwalk$GEOID, own_chg_tract$GEOID[!is.na(own_chg_tract$chg_own)])
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: every crosswalk tract has a tract group with both periods", "0 missing", length(miss_grp),
       length(miss_grp) == 0, stop_if_fail = TRUE)
xg <- own_chg_tract %>% filter(GEOID %in% tract_xwalk$GEOID)
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: crosswalk tracts compared one-to-one / as part of a split or merged group", "reported",
       sprintf("%d / %d", sum(xg$n20 == 1 & xg$n10 == 1), sum(!(xg$n20 == 1 & xg$n10 == 1))), TRUE)
tot_chk <- c(sum(g24$e_own), sum(t24$e_own[t24$GEOID %in% grp20$GEOID]), sum(g19$e_own), sum(t19$e_own[t19$GEOID %in% grp10$GEOID]))
qa_add(5, "Homeownership change: owner households summed over tract groups equal the tract sums, both periods",
       paste(fmt(tot_chk[c(2, 4)]), collapse = " / "), paste(fmt(tot_chk[c(1, 3)]), collapse = " / "),
       tot_chk[1] == tot_chk[2] && tot_chk[3] == tot_chk[4], stop_if_fail = TRUE)

## Working-class tract definition

There is no single standard definition of a working-class neighborhood. Published work defines the working class by education, by occupation or by income, and a smaller set of studies applies those ideas to census tracts. In this analysis, we draw on the following sources.

- **Education.** The Center for American Progress defines the working class as people in the labor force without a four-year college degree ([Rowell 2017](https://www.americanprogressaction.org/article/everyone-know-americas-diverse-working-class/); [Center for American Progress, "Understanding the Working Class and the Challenges It Faces"](https://www.americanprogress.org/article/understanding-the-working-class-and-the-challenges-it-faces/)).
- **Occupation.** Pew Research Center's 2026 study of who sees themselves as working class counts as blue-collar those who do manual or physical labor in manufacturing, mining and construction; agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting; retail and trade; hospitality and service; or transportation ([Pew Research Center 2026](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/08/31/who-sees-themselves-as-working-class/)).
- **Income.** Reardon and Bischoff sort neighborhoods by the ratio of tract median family income to the metro median, from poor (under 0.67) to affluent (1.50 and over), with "low-middle" at 0.80 to 1.00 ([Reardon and Bischoff 2011](https://s4.ad.brown.edu/Projects/Diversity/Data/Report/report111111.pdf)).
- **Census tracts classed directly.** Two published approaches label tracts by the work their residents do. The Public Health Disparities Geocoding Project measures the share of employed residents in working-class occupations, meaning non-supervisory jobs, and treats areas at 66% or more as working-class ([Krieger et al. 2002](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12594195/)). Florida and Adler label a tract by the occupational class (creative, service or working) that holds a plurality of its residents ([Florida and Adler 2018](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/07352166.2017.1360743)). Other studies derive a working-class or blue-collar neighborhood type from cluster analysis ([Morenoff and Tienda 1997](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0002716297551001005); [Delmelle 2016](https://doi.org/10.1080/00045608.2015.1096188)), which gives no cut-off to reuse.

None of these is adopted as is. Each of the tract-level rules rests on occupation alone, and Florida and Adler separate service workers from the working class, while this project counts them in it. In this analysis, a tract must instead look working-class on all three dimensions at once, each measured with an ACS tract table: education as the Center for American Progress defines it, occupation following Pew's list, and income on the Reardon and Bischoff scale. One difference from Pew: the ACS sales-and-office group also covers office and administrative support, so test B is somewhat broader than Pew's list.

**Definition used in this analysis.** A tract is **working-class** when all three tests hold:

- **A. Education**: at least 50% of adults 25 and over have no bachelor's degree: 1 − (B15003_022 + _023 + _024 + _025) ÷ B15003_001.
- **B. Occupation**: at least 50% of employed civilians 16 and over work in service; sales and office; natural resources, construction and maintenance; or production, transportation and material moving occupations: (DP03_0028 + DP03_0029 + DP03_0030 + DP03_0031) ÷ DP03_0026.
- **C. Income**: tract median family income is below the Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim metro median, `r paste0("$", fmt(metro_mfi))` in the 2020–2024 ACS (B19113_001 tract ÷ metro, ratio under 1.00, "low-middle" or lower on the Reardon and Bischoff scale).

A tract with under 100 residents or no published median family income gets no class.

**Borderline tracts.** ACS figures are estimates from a sample of households, so every share comes with a margin of error: the range the true value is likely to fall in (the Census Bureau publishes it at 90% confidence). A tract is **borderline** when its share for test A or test B sits so close to the 50% line that this range crosses it. The tract passes or fails the test on its estimate, but the true share could plausibly be on the other side. For example, a tract where 53% of adults have no bachelor's degree, plus or minus 5 points, passes test A, yet its range of 48% to 58% includes 50%, so it is borderline. Borderline tracts keep the class their estimates give them. The comparison tables also show results without them, to check that a finding does not rest on tracts that could have been classed either way. Test C compares two medians and has no comparable margin here, so it plays no part in the borderline flag.

```{r stage6-working-class}
# =============================================================================
# STAGE 6. WORKING-CLASS TRACTS
# Classifies each crosswalk tract, then prints the sensitivity table (tract
# counts only) before any ADU result is compared across tract classes.
# Stops the knit if: a tract has neither a class nor an "insufficient data" flag.
# =============================================================================
classify_tracts <- function(long, xw) {   # one rule for the six CPAs and citywide
  tc <- component_table(long, "GEOID") %>%
    filter(comp %in% c("pop", "ed_univ", "ed_ba", "emp_occ", "occ_wc", "emp_ind", "ind_wc")) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = comp, values_from = c(estimate, moe))
  med <- long %>% filter(variable %in% c("B19113_001", "B19013_001")) %>%
    distinct(GEOID, variable, estimate) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate)
  xw %>% select(GEOID, CT20, cpa) %>%
    left_join(tc, by = c("GEOID" = "group")) %>%
    left_join(transmute(med, GEOID, mfi = B19113_001, mhi = B19013_001), by = "GEOID") %>%
    mutate(
      share_ba  = estimate_ed_ba / estimate_ed_univ,
      moe_ba    = moe_prop(estimate_ed_ba, estimate_ed_univ, moe_ed_ba, moe_ed_univ),
      share_no_ba = 1 - share_ba,
      share_occ = estimate_occ_wc / estimate_emp_occ,
      moe_occ   = moe_prop(estimate_occ_wc, estimate_emp_occ, moe_occ_wc, moe_emp_occ),
      share_ind = estimate_ind_wc / estimate_emp_ind,
      mfi_ratio = mfi / metro_mfi,
      mhi_ratio = mhi / county_mhi,
      test_A = share_no_ba >= 0.5,
      test_B = share_occ >= 0.5,
      test_C = mfi_ratio < 1,
      test_B_ind = share_ind >= 0.5,
      test_C_hh  = mhi_ratio < 1,
      insufficient    = estimate_pop < 100 | is.na(mfi),
      insufficient_hh = estimate_pop < 100 | is.na(mhi),
      borderline = (abs(share_no_ba - 0.5) <= moe_ba) | (abs(share_occ - 0.5) <= moe_occ),
      wc_rec = !insufficient & test_A & test_B & test_C,
      wc_ind = !insufficient & test_A & test_B_ind & test_C,
      wc_hh  = !insufficient_hh & test_A & test_B & test_C_hh,
      class = case_when(insufficient ~ "Insufficient data",
                        wc_rec ~ "Working-class",
                        TRUE ~ "Other"))
}
tract_class <- classify_tracts(acs_long, tract_xwalk)
qa_add(6, "Every crosswalk tract has a class or an insufficient-data flag", "317",
       sum(tract_class$class %in% c("Working-class", "Other", "Insufficient data")),
       all(tract_class$class %in% c("Working-class", "Other", "Insufficient data")) &&
         !any(is.na(tract_class$test_A[!tract_class$insufficient])) &&
         !any(is.na(tract_class$test_B[!tract_class$insufficient])), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
insuff <- tract_class %>% filter(insufficient)
qa_add(6, "Tracts with insufficient data (expected 9800.21, 2218.10, 2247.02, 2372.02)", "4",
       paste0(nrow(insuff), " (", paste(sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(insuff$CT20) / 100), collapse = ", "), ")"),
       setequal(insuff$CT20, c("980021", "221810", "224702", "237202")))

# Citywide classification with the same rule, for the citywide map
acs_long_city <- acs_long_all %>% inner_join(select(city_xwalk, GEOID, cpa), by = "GEOID")
qa_add(6, "City tracts missing from the ACS pull", "0", length(setdiff(city_xwalk$GEOID, acs_long_city$GEOID)),
       all(city_xwalk$GEOID %in% acs_long_city$GEOID), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
tract_class_city <- classify_tracts(acs_long_city, city_xwalk)
same_cls <- tract_class %>% select(GEOID, class, test_A, test_B, test_C, borderline) %>%
  inner_join(select(tract_class_city, GEOID, class2 = class, A2 = test_A, B2 = test_B, C2 = test_C, bl2 = borderline), by = "GEOID")
qa_add(6, "Citywide classification matches the six-CPA classification tract by tract", "317 of 317",
       paste(sum(same_cls$class == same_cls$class2 & same_cls$test_A %in% same_cls$A2 & same_cls$test_B %in% same_cls$B2 &
                   same_cls$test_C %in% same_cls$C2 & same_cls$borderline %in% same_cls$bl2), "of", nrow(tract_class)),
       nrow(same_cls) == nrow(tract_class) && all(same_cls$class == same_cls$class2) &&
         identical(same_cls$test_A, same_cls$A2) && identical(same_cls$test_B, same_cls$B2) &&
         identical(same_cls$test_C, same_cls$C2) && identical(same_cls$borderline, same_cls$bl2), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
```

### Sensitivity: tract counts under the rule and two alternatives

A definition built from three tests could give a different answer if any one test were measured another way. This table checks how much the result depends on those choices. It shows **tract counts only**: the rule was fixed before any ADU result was compared across tract classes. Reading across the columns:

- **A. Education, B. Occupation, C. Family income below metro**: tracts that pass each test taken alone.
- **Working-class: A + B + C (rule used)**: tracts that pass all three, the definition used in this analysis.
- **Borderline**: tracts whose share for test A or B is within its margin of error of 50%.
- **Alt. B: industry**: an alternative way to measure test B. It counts workers by the industry they work in (construction, manufacturing, trade, transportation, hospitality and other services) in place of the occupation they hold. **Working-class with industry B** is the number of tracts classed working-class if this measure replaces test B.
- **Alt. C: household income below county**: an alternative way to measure test C. It compares the tract's median household income with the Los Angeles County median, `r paste0("$", fmt(county_mhi))` in the 2020–2024 ACS (B19013_001), in place of median family income with the metro median. **Working-class with household-income C** is the number of tracts classed working-class if this measure replaces test C.

If the three "working-class" columns were close, the choice of measure would matter little. Where they differ, the definition is sensitive to that choice in that CPA.

```{r stage6-sensitivity}
sens <- tract_class %>%
  mutate(cpa = factor(cpa, levels = focus_cpas)) %>%
  group_by(cpa) %>%
  summarise(Tracts = n(),
            `Insufficient data` = sum(insufficient),
            `A. Education` = sum(test_A & !insufficient, na.rm = TRUE),
            `B. Occupation` = sum(test_B & !insufficient, na.rm = TRUE),
            `C. Family income below metro` = sum(test_C & !insufficient, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Working-class: A + B + C (rule used)` = sum(wc_rec, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Borderline (A or B interval includes 50%)` = sum(borderline & !insufficient, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Alt. B: industry` = sum(test_B_ind & !insufficient, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Working-class with industry B` = sum(wc_ind, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Alt. C: household income below county` = sum(test_C_hh & !insufficient_hh, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Working-class with household-income C` = sum(wc_hh, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
sens_total <- sens %>% summarise(across(-cpa, sum)) %>% mutate(cpa = "All six CPAs")
bind_rows(mutate(sens, cpa = as.character(cpa)), sens_total) %>%
  rename(CPA = cpa) %>%
  tbl(caption = "Census tracts passing each working-class test, alone and together (census tracts)",
      note = paste0("ACS 2020–2024 5-year. A: B15003_001, _022–_025. B: DP03_0026, DP03_0028–_0031. ",
                    "C: B19113_001, tract ÷ Los Angeles–Long Beach–Anaheim metro ($", fmt(metro_mfi), "). ",
                    "Alt. B: DP03_0033–_0038, _0043, _0044 ÷ DP03_0032. ",
                    "Alt. C: B19013_001, tract ÷ Los Angeles County ($", fmt(county_mhi), "). ",
                    "Test counts exclude tracts with insufficient data (under 100 residents or no published median)."))
```

`r sum(tract_class$wc_rec)` of `r nrow(tract_class) - sum(tract_class$insufficient)` classifiable tracts pass all three tests, and `r sum(tract_class$borderline & !tract_class$insufficient, na.rm = TRUE)` are borderline on test A or B. Four tracts have no published median family income in the 2020–2024 file and get no class: `r paste(sprintf("%.2f", as.numeric(insuff$CT20) / 100), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r map-helpers}
# Shared web-map helpers, used from here on (the citywide working-class map below,
# the citywide section and the CPA sections).
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(leaflet); library(htmltools); library(htmlwidgets); library(plotly) })
city_fit_sf <- cpa_sf %>% filter(!cpa %in% c("Port of Los Angeles", "Los Angeles International Airport"))   # opening extent of the citywide maps
# ---- Map helpers --------------------------------------------------------------
bm_for <- function(geom_ft, tiles = 4) {
  bb <- st_bbox(st_transform(geom_ft, crs_web))
  light_basemap(bb, zoom = zoom_for(bb, tiles = tiles))
}
leaflet_base <- function(height = 560, bm_key = NULL) {
  m <- leaflet(height = height, options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE, zoomSnap = 0.25, zoomDelta = 0.5)) %>%
    addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") %>%
    addTiles(urlTemplate = "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/Canvas/World_Light_Gray_Reference/MapServer/tile/{z}/{y}/{x}",
             attribution = "Esri, HERE, Garmin, (c) OpenStreetMap contributors")
  if (!is.null(bm_key)) m <- add_bm(m, bm_key)
  m
}
# ---- Embedded basemap under every web map ------------------------------------
# The web maps load the Esri tiles over the internet. Where a viewer blocks
# outside images, or the page is opened offline, the tiles never arrive, so each
# web map also carries the same Esri basemap (base plus labels, built from the
# cached tiles like the static maps) as one image under the live tiles. The live
# tiles cover it when they load; failed tiles stay hidden, so it shows through.
merc2ll <- function(x, y) c(lng = x / 6378137 * 180 / pi, lat = (2 * atan(exp(y / 6378137)) - pi / 2) * 180 / pi)
bm_embed <- function(geom_ft, tiles, quality = 0.8) {
  bb <- st_bbox(st_transform(geom_ft, crs_web))
  bm <- light_basemap(bb, zoom = zoom_for(bb, tiles = tiles))
  f <- tempfile(fileext = ".jpg"); jpeg::writeJPEG(bm$img, f, quality = quality)
  sw <- merc2ll(bm$ext[["xmin"]], bm$ext[["ymin"]]); ne <- merc2ll(bm$ext[["xmax"]], bm$ext[["ymax"]])
  list(url = paste0("data:image/jpeg;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(f)),
       bounds = list(c(sw[["lat"]], sw[["lng"]]), c(ne[["lat"]], ne[["lng"]])),
       px = dim(bm$img)[2:1], blank = mean(bm$img) > 0.999)
}
cpa_key <- function(cc) gsub("[^a-z]", "", tolower(cc))
bm_store <- list(city = bm_embed(st_buffer(st_union(cpa_sf), 10560), tiles = 8))
for (cc in focus_cpas) {
  frame_cc <- st_union(c(st_geometry(filter(cpa_sf, cpa == cc)),
                         st_geometry(filter(tracts_sf, CT20 %in% tract_xwalk$CT20[tract_xwalk$cpa == cc]))))
  bm_store[[cpa_key(cc)]] <- bm_embed(st_buffer(frame_cc, 5280), tiles = 5)
}
n_blank <- sum(vapply(bm_store, `[[`, TRUE, "blank"))
qa_add(6, "Embedded basemap images built for the City and the six CPAs (none blank)", "0 blank",
       paste(n_blank, "blank"), n_blank == 0,
       reason = if (n_blank > 0) "The Esri tiles could not be fetched when the report was knit (offline?). The web maps still show the live tiles when the page is opened online." else NA_character_)
add_bm <- function(m, key) {
  onRender(m, "
    function(el, x, data) {
      var b = window.aduBasemaps && window.aduBasemaps[data.key];
      if (!b) return;
      var map = this;
      if (!map.getPane('bmEmbed')) {
        var p = map.createPane('bmEmbed'); p.style.zIndex = 150; p.style.pointerEvents = 'none';
      }
      L.imageOverlay(b.url, b.bounds, {pane: 'bmEmbed', interactive: false}).addTo(map);
    }", data = list(key = key))
}
fit_to <- function(m, geom_ft) {    # open the map on the CPA
  b <- st_bbox(st_transform(geom_ft, crs_web))
  fitBounds(m, b[["xmin"]], b[["ymin"]], b[["xmax"]], b[["ymax"]])
}
label_style <- list("font-size" = "11px", "font-weight" = "bold", "color" = "#222222",
                    "text-shadow" = "0 0 3px #FFFFFF, 0 0 3px #FFFFFF, 0 0 2px #FFFFFF")
to_ll <- function(x, digits = 6) {   # web-map geometry with rounded coordinates (6 decimals ~ 10 cm; 5 ~ 1 m) to keep the page small
  x <- st_transform(x, crs_web)
  st_geometry(x) <- st_as_sfc(st_as_binary(st_geometry(x), precision = 10^digits), crs = crs_web)
  x
}
hatch_lines <- function(poly, n = 70) {           # diagonal hatching clipped to a polygon
  if (length(poly) == 0 || all(st_is_empty(poly))) return(st_sfc(crs = st_crs(poly)))
  bb <- st_bbox(poly); w <- bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]]; h <- bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]
  step <- max(w, h) / n
  offs <- seq(-h, w, by = step)
  lines <- lapply(offs, function(o) st_linestring(rbind(c(bb[["xmin"]] + o, bb[["ymin"]]),
                                                        c(bb[["xmin"]] + o + h, bb[["ymax"]]))))
  st_intersection(st_sfc(lines, crs = st_crs(poly)), st_union(poly))
}
# ---- Working-class hover: the three test values, each marked pass or fail -----
wc_cols <- c("Working-class" = "#C2662D", "Other" = "#6BAED6", "Insufficient data" = "#D9D9D9")
wc_pal <- function(x) unname(wc_cols[x])
mark <- function(ok) ifelse(is.na(ok), "",
                            ifelse(ok, "<span style='color:#1a7f37;font-weight:bold'>&#10003; pass</span>",
                                   "<span style='color:#C0392B;font-weight:bold'>&#10007; fail</span>"))
fails_txt <- function(d) {
  nm <- c(A = "A (education)", B = "B (occupation)", C = "C (income)")
  f <- cbind(A = !d$test_A, B = !d$test_B, C = !d$test_C)
  apply(f, 1, function(r) { x <- nm[names(r)[r %in% TRUE]]
    if (length(x) <= 1) paste(x, collapse = "") else paste(paste(head(x, -1), collapse = ", "), "and", tail(x, 1)) })
}
wc_hover <- function(d, cls = d$class, cpa_name = NULL) {
  few <- (d$estimate_pop < 100) %in% TRUE | is.na(d$estimate_pop)   # values from under 100 residents are not shown
  a <- ifelse(few, NA, d$share_no_ba); am <- ifelse(few, NA, d$moe_ba)
  b <- ifelse(few, NA, d$share_occ);   bm <- ifelse(few, NA, d$moe_occ)
  p1 <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "n/a", paste0(fmt(100 * x, 1), "%"))
  pm <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", paste0(" &plusmn; ", fmt(100 * x, 1), " pts"))
  status <- case_when(
    cls == "Insufficient data" ~ paste0("<b>No class</b>: ", ifelse(few, "under 100 residents", "no published median family income")),
    cls == "Working-class" ~ "<b>Working-class</b>: passes A, B and C",
    TRUE ~ paste0("<b>Other (not working-class)</b>: fails ", fails_txt(d)))
  bl <- ifelse(cls != "Insufficient data" & d$borderline %in% TRUE,
               "<br><i>Borderline: the 90% interval for A or B includes 50%</i>", "")
  paste0("<b>Tract ", d$LABEL, "</b>", if (!is.null(cpa_name)) paste0(" &middot; ", cpa_name) else "", "<br>", status, bl,
         "<br><b>A. Adults 25+ with no bachelor's degree</b><br>", p1(a), pm(am), " &middot; needs 50% or more &middot; ",
         mark(ifelse(few, NA, d$test_A)),
         "<br><b>B. Workers in service, sales and office, construction,</b><br><b>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;production or transport jobs</b><br>",
         p1(b), pm(bm), " &middot; needs 50% or more &middot; ", mark(ifelse(few, NA, d$test_B)),
         "<br><b>C. Median family income &divide; metro median</b><br>",
         ifelse(is.na(d$mfi), "not published",
                paste0("$", fmt(d$mfi), " &divide; $", fmt(metro_mfi), " = ", fmt(d$mfi_ratio, 2))),
         " &middot; needs under 1.00 &middot; ", mark(d$test_C))
}

### Working-class census tracts across Los Angeles, by definition

The map applies the rule and the two alternatives from the table above to every census tract in the City, so the effect of each choice can be seen across Los Angeles and not only in the six candidate CPAs. Use the control to switch definitions, to show the tracts whose class changes under an alternative, or to show which tests the other tracts fail under the rule.

```{r wc-city-map}
pat_levels <- c("Fails income (C) only", "Fails income and one of education or occupation",
                "Fails all three tests", "Fails education or occupation, passes income")
pat_cols <- setNames(c("#9ECAE1", "#4292C6", "#08306B", "#74C476"), pat_levels)
cls3 <- function(ins, wc) case_when(ins ~ "Insufficient data", wc %in% TRUE ~ "Working-class", TRUE ~ "Other")
chg_levels <- c("Working-class under all three definitions", "Not working-class under all three",
                "Changes with industry B only", "Changes with household-income C only", "Changes with both alternatives",
                "Insufficient data under the rule")
chg_cols <- setNames(c("#E8C9B5", "#C6DBEF", "#7B3294", "#008837", "#D7191C", "#D9D9D9"), chg_levels)
tc_city <- tract_class_city %>%
  mutate(pattern = case_when(class != "Other" ~ NA_character_,
                             !test_A & !test_B & !test_C ~ "Fails all three tests",
                             !test_C & test_A & test_B ~ "Fails income (C) only",
                             test_C ~ "Fails education or occupation, passes income",
                             TRUE ~ "Fails income and one of education or occupation"),
         class_ind = cls3(insufficient, wc_ind), class_hh = cls3(insufficient_hh, wc_hh),
         d_ind = class_ind != class, d_hh = class_hh != class,
         change = case_when(class == "Insufficient data" ~ chg_levels[6],
                            d_ind & d_hh ~ chg_levels[5], d_ind ~ chg_levels[3], d_hh ~ chg_levels[4],
                            class == "Working-class" ~ chg_levels[1], TRUE ~ chg_levels[2]))
qa_add(6, "Citywide working-class map: every classifiable City tract has all three test results", "0 missing",
       paste(sum(tc_city$class != "Insufficient data" & (is.na(tc_city$test_A) | is.na(tc_city$test_B) | is.na(tc_city$test_C))), "missing"),
       !any(tc_city$class != "Insufficient data" & (is.na(tc_city$test_A) | is.na(tc_city$test_B) | is.na(tc_city$test_C))),
       stop_if_fail = TRUE)
qa_add(6, "Citywide working-class map: failure patterns cover every other tract exactly once", sum(tc_city$class == "Other"),
       sum(!is.na(tc_city$pattern)), sum(!is.na(tc_city$pattern)) == sum(tc_city$class == "Other"), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
six_def <- tc_city %>% filter(cpa %in% focus_cpas)
qa_add(6, "Citywide working-class map: working-class tracts in the six CPAs under each definition match the sensitivity table (rule / industry B / household-income C)",
       paste(sens_total$`Working-class: A + B + C (rule used)`, sens_total$`Working-class with industry B`,
             sens_total$`Working-class with household-income C`, sep = " / "),
       paste(sum(six_def$class == "Working-class"), sum(six_def$class_ind == "Working-class"), sum(six_def$class_hh == "Working-class"), sep = " / "),
       sum(six_def$class == "Working-class") == sens_total$`Working-class: A + B + C (rule used)` &&
         sum(six_def$class_ind == "Working-class") == sens_total$`Working-class with industry B` &&
         sum(six_def$class_hh == "Working-class") == sens_total$`Working-class with household-income C`, stop_if_fail = TRUE)
qa_add(6, "Citywide working-class map: the change categories cover every City tract exactly once", nrow(tc_city),
       sum(tc_city$change %in% chg_levels), all(tc_city$change %in% chg_levels), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
c5_sf <- tracts_sf %>% select(CT20, LABEL) %>% inner_join(tc_city, by = "CT20") %>%

qa_add(6, "Citywide working-class map has every City tract", nrow(city_xwalk), nrow(c5_sf), nrow(c5_sf) == nrow(city_xwalk), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
fill_why <- case_when(c5_sf$class == "Working-class" ~ "#F3D5BF",
                      c5_sf$class == "Insufficient data" ~ "#D9D9D9",
                      TRUE ~ unname(pat_cols[c5_sf$pattern]))
gid <- function(v) as.list(setNames(v, c5_sf$GEOID))
# Six income categories of Reardon and Bischoff (2011), on the ratio of tract to area median income
inc_breaks <- c(0.67, 0.80, 1.00, 1.25, 1.50)
inc_labs <- c("Poor (under 0.67)", "Low income (0.67 to 0.80)", "Low-middle income (0.80 to 1.00)", "High-middle income (1.00 to 1.25)",

inc_cols <- c("#B2182B", "#EF8A62", "#FDDBC7", "#D1E5F0", "#67A9CF", "#2166AC")

cols_c5 <- list(rec = gid(wc_pal(c5_sf$class)), ind = gid(wc_pal(c5_sf$class_ind)), hh = gid(wc_pal(c5_sf$class_hh)),

bl_ll <- c5_sf %>% filter(class != "Insufficient data", borderline %in% TRUE)
m_c5 <- leaflet_base(height = 660, bm_key = "city") %>% fit_to(city_fit_sf) %>%
  addPolygons(data = c5_sf, layerId = ~GEOID, fillColor = wc_pal(c5_sf$class), fillOpacity = 0.7, color = "#FFFFFF", weight = 0.4,
              label = lapply(paste0(wc_hover(c5_sf, cpa_name = c5_sf$cpa), alt_hover), HTML), group = "c5") %>%
  addPolygons(data = bl_ll, fill = FALSE, color = "#222222", weight = 1.2, dashArray = "3,3",
              options = pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)) %>%   # outline only: hover reaches the layer below
  addPolygons(data = to_ll(st_simplify(cpa_sf, preserveTopology = TRUE, dTolerance = 50), digits = 5),
              fill = FALSE, color = "#555555", weight = 0.7,
              options = pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)) %>%   # outline only: hover reaches the layer below
  addPolygons(data = to_ll(filter(cpa_sf, cpa %in% focus_cpas), digits = 5), fill = FALSE, color = "black", weight = 2.2,
              options = pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)) %>%   # outline only: hover reaches the layer below
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = unname(wc_cols), labels = names(wc_cols), opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Tract class", className = "info legend leg-cls") %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = unname(chg_cols), labels = names(chg_cols), opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Class under the rule and the two alternatives", className = "info legend leg-chg") %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = c("#F3D5BF", unname(pat_cols), "#D9D9D9"),
            labels = c("Working-class", pat_levels, "Insufficient data"), opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Why a tract is not working-class (A + B + C)", className = "info legend leg-why") %>%
  addLegend("bottomright", colors = c(inc_cols, "#D9D9D9"), labels = c(inc_labs, "Not published"), opacity = 0.8,
            title = "Tract median household income &divide; county median", className = "info legend leg-inc") %>%
  onRender("
    function(el, x, data) {
      var map = this, nm = el.id;
      var opts = [['rec', 'A + B + C (rule used)'], ['ind', 'Industry in place of occupation (alt. B)'],
                  ['hh', 'Household income against the county median (alt. C)']];
      var cmp = [['chg', 'Tracts that change class under an alternative'], ['why', 'A + B + C: which tests other tracts fail'],
                 ['inc', 'Alt. C income measure in six income categories']];
      var ctrl = L.control({position: 'topright'});
      ctrl.onAdd = function() {
        var div = L.DomUtil.create('div', 'leaflet-bar');
        div.style.background = 'white'; div.style.padding = '6px 8px'; div.style.fontSize = '12px'; div.style.maxWidth = '290px';
        var h = '<b>Working-class definition</b><br>';
        opts.forEach(function(o, i) { h += '<label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"' + nm + '_v\" value=\"' + o[0] + '\"' + (i === 0 ? ' checked' : '') + '> ' + o[1] + '</label><br>'; });
        h += '<b>Compare</b><br>';
        cmp.forEach(function(o) { h += '<label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"' + nm + '_v\" value=\"' + o[0] + '\"> ' + o[1] + '</label><br>'; });
        h += '<div class=\"wc-n\" style=\"margin-top:4px; color:#444;\"></div>';
        div.innerHTML = h; L.DomEvent.disableClickPropagation(div);
        return div;
      };
      ctrl.addTo(map);
      function update() {
        var v = el.querySelector('input[name=\"' + nm + '_v\"]:checked').value;
        var cols = data.cols[v];
        Object.keys(cols).forEach(function(id) {
          var l = map.layerManager.getLayer('shape', id);
          if (l) l.setStyle({fillColor: cols[id]});
        });
        var leg = (v === 'chg' || v === 'why' || v === 'inc') ? v : 'cls';
        ['cls', 'chg', 'why', 'inc'].forEach(function(k) {
          el.querySelectorAll('.leg-' + k).forEach(function(d) { d.style.display = k === leg ? '' : 'none'; });
        });
        el.querySelector('.wc-n').innerHTML = data.counts[v] || '';
      }
      el.addEventListener('change', update);
      update();
    }", data = list(cols = cols_c5, counts = list(
      rec = sprintf("%s working-class, %s other, %s no class", fmt(sum(tc_city$class == "Working-class")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class == "Other")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class == "Insufficient data"))),
      ind = sprintf("%s working-class, %s other, %s no class", fmt(sum(tc_city$class_ind == "Working-class")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class_ind == "Other")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class_ind == "Insufficient data"))),
      hh = sprintf("%s working-class, %s other, %s no class", fmt(sum(tc_city$class_hh == "Working-class")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class_hh == "Other")), fmt(sum(tc_city$class_hh == "Insufficient data"))),
      chg = sprintf("%s tracts change class under at least one alternative", fmt(sum(tc_city$change %in% chg_levels[3:5]))))))
def_row <- function(lab, cl) {
  tibble(Definition = lab, `Working-class` = fmt(sum(cl == "Working-class")), Other = fmt(sum(cl == "Other")),
         `No class (insufficient data)` = fmt(sum(cl == "Insufficient data")),

         `Working-class under the rule, not here` = fmt(sum(cl != "Working-class" & tc_city$class == "Working-class")),
         `Working-class in the six candidate CPAs` = fmt(sum(cl == "Working-class" & tc_city$cpa %in% focus_cpas)))
}
def_tab <- bind_rows(def_row("A + B + C (rule used)", tc_city$class),

tagList(tags$p(tags$b("Working-class census tracts in Los Angeles under each definition")),

                      "Dashed outline: borderline under the rule (the 90% interval for A or B includes 50%). ",

inc_tab <- tc_city %>% mutate(cat = as.character(inc_cat(mhi_ratio)), cat = factor(coalesce(cat, "Not published"), levels = c(inc_labs, "Not published"))) %>%

qa_add(6, "Income categories: every City tract falls in one category or is not published", nrow(tc_city), sum(inc_tab$`City tracts`),

def_tab %>%

                    fmt(county_mhi), "). No class: under 100 residents, or no published median for the income measure the definition uses."),

Alt. C counts a tract as passing the income test when the ratio is under 1.00, that is, in the first three categories. Choose \"Alt. C income measure in six income categories\" on the map above to see them."),

### Working Class Definition (A+B+C) in Application in Los Angeles

```{r wc-app-data}
n_city <- nrow(tc_city); n_wc_c <- sum(tc_city$class == "Working-class")
n_oth_c <- sum(tc_city$class == "Other"); n_ins_c <- sum(tc_city$class == "Insufficient data")
n_fail <- c(A = sum(tc_city$class == "Other" & !tc_city$test_A), B = sum(tc_city$class == "Other" & !tc_city$test_B),
            C = sum(tc_city$class == "Other" & !tc_city$test_C))
pat_n <- function(d, p) sum(d$pattern %in% p)
top_cpas <- function(p, k = 3) {
  tc_city %>% filter(pattern %in% p) %>% count(cpa, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = k) %>%
    summarise(txt = paste0(cpa, " (", n, ")", collapse = "; ")) %>% pull(txt)
}
six_oth <- tc_city %>% filter(cpa %in% focus_cpas, class == "Other")
n_bl_oth <- sum(tc_city$class == "Other" & tc_city$borderline %in% TRUE)
near_A <- abs(tc_city$share_no_ba - 0.5) <= tc_city$moe_ba; near_B <- abs(tc_city$share_occ - 0.5) <= tc_city$moe_occ
could_wc <- tc_city$class == "Other" & tc_city$test_C & (tc_city$test_A | near_A) & (tc_city$test_B | near_B)   # pass C; miss A or B only within the MOE
n_could <- sum(could_wc, na.rm = TRUE); n_could_six <- sum(could_wc & tc_city$cpa %in% focus_cpas, na.rm = TRUE)
n_bl_failC <- sum(tc_city$class == "Other" & tc_city$borderline %in% TRUE & !tc_city$test_C)
```

Of the `r fmt(n_city)` census tracts in the City, `r fmt(n_wc_c)` (`r pct(n_wc_c / (n_city - n_ins_c))` of those with data) are working-class, `r fmt(n_oth_c)` are other, and `r n_ins_c` have too few residents or no published median family income to classify. Of the `r fmt(n_oth_c)` other tracts, `r fmt(n_fail[["C"]])` fail the income test (median family income at or above the metro median of $`r fmt(metro_mfi)`), `r fmt(n_fail[["A"]])` fail the education test and `r fmt(n_fail[["B"]])` fail the occupation test. The tests overlap heavily: `r fmt(pat_n(tc_city, "Fails all three tests"))` other tracts fail all three. Only `r fmt(n_could)` other tracts (`r n_could_six` of them in the six candidate CPAs) pass the income test and miss A or B by no more than the margin of error, so their class could change with a different sample. More other tracts, `r fmt(n_bl_oth)`, are borderline on A or B, but `r fmt(n_bl_failC)` of them also fail the income test, so the margin of error on A or B does not change their class. In the six candidate CPAs, `r nrow(six_oth)` tracts are other: `r pat_n(six_oth, "Fails all three tests")` fail all three tests, `r pat_n(six_oth, "Fails income (C) only")` fail only the income test, `r pat_n(six_oth, "Fails income and one of education or occupation")` fail income and one other test, and `r pat_n(six_oth, "Fails education or occupation, passes income")` pass income but fail education or occupation.

```{r wc-app-venn, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.6}
# Venn diagram: which of the three tests the tracts that are not working-class fail
venn_counts <- function(d, where) {
  d <- d %>% filter(class == "Other"); fa <- !d$test_A; fb <- !d$test_B; fc <- !d$test_C
  tibble(panel = where,
         region = c("A", "B", "C", "AB", "AC", "BC", "ABC"),
         n = c(sum(fa & !fb & !fc), sum(!fa & fb & !fc), sum(!fa & !fb & fc), sum(fa & fb & !fc),
               sum(fa & !fb & fc), sum(!fa & fb & fc), sum(fa & fb & fc)),
         x = c(-1.05, 1.05, 0, 0, -0.68, 0.68, 0), y = c(0.62, 0.62, -1.18, 0.82, -0.36, -0.36, 0.05),
         tot_A = sum(fa), tot_B = sum(fb), tot_C = sum(fc), n_other = nrow(d))
}
vn <- bind_rows(venn_counts(tc_city, "City of Los Angeles"), venn_counts(filter(tc_city, cpa %in% focus_cpas), "Six candidate CPAs")) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = c("City of Los Angeles", "Six candidate CPAs")))
vn_tot <- vn %>% group_by(panel) %>% summarise(n_sum = sum(n), n_other = first(n_other), tot_A = first(tot_A), tot_B = first(tot_B), tot_C = first(tot_C), .groups = "drop")
qa_add(6, "Venn diagram: the seven regions sum to the tracts that are not working-class (City / six CPAs)",
       paste(vn_tot$n_other, collapse = " / "), paste(vn_tot$n_sum, collapse = " / "), all(vn_tot$n_sum == vn_tot$n_other), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
qa_add(6, "Venn diagram: City and six-CPA totals match the write-up above", paste(n_oth_c, nrow(six_oth), sep = " / "),
       paste(vn_tot$n_other, collapse = " / "), vn_tot$n_other[1] == n_oth_c && vn_tot$n_other[2] == nrow(six_oth), stop_if_fail = TRUE)
circ <- function(cx, cy, set) { th <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 181); tibble(x = cx + cos(th), y = cy + sin(th), set = set) }
circles <- bind_rows(circ(-0.5, 0.3, "A"), circ(0.5, 0.3, "B"), circ(0, -0.55, "C"))
circles <- bind_rows(mutate(circles, panel = levels(vn$panel)[1]), mutate(circles, panel = levels(vn$panel)[2])) %>%
  mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = levels(vn$panel)))
set_lab <- vn_tot %>% rowwise() %>% reframe(panel,
  x = c(-1.25, 1.25, 0), y = c(1.52, 1.52, -1.78),
  label = c(paste0("Fails A: education\n(", fmt(tot_A), " tracts)"), paste0("Fails B: occupation\n(", fmt(tot_B), " tracts)"),
            paste0("Fails C: income\n(", fmt(tot_C), " tracts)")))
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = circles, aes(x, y, group = set, fill = set), alpha = 0.28, color = "grey25", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(data = vn, aes(x, y, label = fmt(n)), size = 5, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = set_lab, aes(x, y, label = label), size = 3.6, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = vn_tot, aes(x = 0, y = -2.25, label = paste0(fmt(n_other), " tracts are not working-class")), size = 3.6, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(A = "#4C78A8", B = "#F58518", C = "#54A24B"), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~panel) + coord_equal(xlim = c(-2.2, 2.2), ylim = c(-2.4, 1.85)) +
  labs(title = "Which tests do the tracts that are not working-class fail?",
       caption = paste0("Each tract that is not working-class fails at least one test; a number in an overlap counts tracts that fail both (or all three) tests.\n",
                        "A: under 50% of adults lack a bachelor's degree. B: under 50% of workers hold the occupations in test B. C: median family income at or above the metro median.\n",
                        "Working-class tracts pass all three tests and sit outside the circles. Circle sizes are not to scale. ACS 2020–2024 5-year.")) +
  theme_void() + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),

# ---- Eligibility flags on the six-CPA parcels ---------------------------------
# Four tiers (protocol addendum 2.1). A: 4,000 sq ft floor, no screen (new). B: 4,500 sq ft
# floor, no screen (was A). C: B less hillside-fire lots, except in the two exempt CPAs
# (was B). D: A less hillside-fire lots everywhere, with no exemption (new).
prop_sf <- prop_sf %>%
  mutate(is_sf = land_use == "Single-family",
         is_mf = str_starts(land_use, "Multi-family"),
         hf_all = in_hill & in_fire,                # in both layers, exempt CPAs included
         big4 = lot_sqft >= 4000, big45 = lot_sqft >= 4500,
         sfA = is_sf & big4,  mfA = is_mf & big4,
         sfB = is_sf & big45, mfB = is_mf & big45,
         sfC = sfB & !hillside_fire, mfC = mfB & !hillside_fire,
         sfD = sfA & !hf_all, mfD = mfA & !hf_all,
         eligA = sfA | mfA, eligB = sfB | mfB, eligC = sfC | mfC, eligD = sfD | mfD)
tier_def <- tribble(~tier, ~floor, ~screen,
  "A", "4,000 sq ft", "None",
  "B", "4,500 sq ft", "None",
  "C", "4,500 sq ft", "Removes hillside-fire lots, except in Northeast Los Angeles and Silver Lake - Echo Park - Elysian Valley",
  "D", "4,000 sq ft", "Removes hillside-fire lots everywhere, with no exemption")
tier_ok <- st_drop_geometry(prop_sf) %>% group_by(cpa) %>%
  summarise(A = sum(eligA), B = sum(eligB), C = sum(eligC), D = sum(eligD), flagged = sum(eligA & hf_all), .groups = "drop")
qa_add(7, "Eligibility tiers: A >= B >= C and A >= D in every CPA; D = A where no eligible lot is in both layers", "holds",
       if (with(tier_ok, all(A >= B & B >= C & A >= D & (flagged > 0 | D == A)))) "holds" else "violated",
       with(tier_ok, all(A >= B & B >= C & A >= D & (flagged > 0 | D == A))), stop_if_fail = TRUE)

# From here on `adu` holds every ADU, whatever its tag: LADBS permitted (2017 to present),

# ---- Summaries reused by the CPA sections and the selection section ----------
land_summary <- function(cc) {
  d <- st_drop_geometry(prop_sf) %>% filter(cpa == cc)
  tibble(cpa = cc, area_sqft = cpa_sf$area_sqft[cpa_sf$cpa == cc],
         r1 = nrow(d), r2 = sum(d$is_sf), r_mf = sum(d$is_mf),
         r6a = sum(d$land_use == "Multi-family, 2-4 units"), r6b = sum(d$land_use == "Multi-family, 5+ units"),
         sfA = sum(d$sfA), mfA = sum(d$mfA), eA = sum(d$eligA), sfB = sum(d$sfB), mfB = sum(d$mfB), eB = sum(d$eligB),
         sfC = sum(d$sfC), mfC = sum(d$mfC), eC = sum(d$eligC), sfD = sum(d$sfD), mfD = sum(d$mfD), eD = sum(d$eligD),
         older = sum(d$older_adu, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(rmC = eB - eC, rmD = eA - eD)
}
adu_summary <- function(d) {
  tibble(projects = nrow(d), units = sum(d$units),
         completed = sum(d$units[d$status == "Completed"]),
         in_progress = sum(d$units[d$status == "In progress"]),
         stalled = sum(d$units[d$status == "Stalled"]),
         outside_A = sum(d$units[d$outside_A]), outside_B = sum(d$units[d$outside_B]),
         outside_C = sum(d$units[d$outside_C]), outside_D = sum(d$units[d$outside_D]),
         properties = n_distinct(d$prop_id[!is.na(d$prop_id)]) + sum(is.na(d$prop_id)),
         prop_sf = n_distinct(d$prop_id[d$property_type == "Single-family"]),
         prop_mf = n_distinct(d$prop_id[d$property_type == "Multi-family" & !is.na(d$prop_id)]) +
           sum(d$property_type == "Multi-family" & is.na(d$prop_id)),
         units_sf = sum(d$units[d$property_type == "Single-family"]),
         units_mf = sum(d$units[d$property_type == "Multi-family"]))
}
land_tbl <- map_dfr(focus_cpas, land_summary)
